reason: It survives the transfer/leakage lens, but the gain is smaller and more fragile than claimed. The three leak channels do not apply. (1) The node count is bit-identical, so the node multiplier does not move. (2) Topology and edge probabilities are unchanged, so the in-sample edge network is trusted no more than before. (3) The sub-voxel part of the coordinates comes only from GT-free linefit smoothing of integer detector peaks. If anything, in-sample peaks sitting on GT integer voxels bias the local test TOWARD rounding. Stress test on the same 199-video tail, adding 1 um/axis Gaussian noise to mimic worse localisation on unseen embryos: the float gain grows instead of shrinking, +0.0023 overall (6bba +0.0022, 44b6 +0.0028; the base score is 0.880 instead of 0.902). The mechanism is generic: rounding is independent quantisation noise that flips near-tie matches. Now the fragility. Float minus round is dTP +70 / dFP -190 on 199 videos. 44b6 contributes only dTP +13 / dFP -31. Its +0.00195 comes entirely from 5 overlapping crops (top-5 +0.00201, the other 66 crops -0.00006), so it is roughly one independent observation of one recording, not 71. On 6bba, the top-5 videos give +0.00105 and the other 123 give +0.00069 (win/lose 51/34). The robust expectation for an unseen embryo is therefore about +0.0007 to +0.0015, not a firm +0.0018. The one real transfer hazard is server-side parsing. Truncation measured -0.0047 on 6bba but +0.0002 on 44b6. If the public embryo behaves like 44b6, a truncating server scores the same as today on public and loses about 0.004 on the 71% private split. So the proposed probe rule ('same score = server rounds, harmless, keep') is unsafe.
fix_if_any: (a) Ship the truncation-proof encoding w = round(v) + clip(round(v - round(v), 3), 0, 0.499), clipped at >= 0, written as %.3f for every node coordinate. floor(w) == round(w) == round(v), so a rounding or int-casting server scores exactly like today, and a Float64 server gets most of the gain. Measured on 199 videos: +0.0019 overall, 6bba +0.00195 (win/lose 50/16), 44b6 +0.00163. It adds a mean +0.125 voxel bias per axis (about 0.2 um in z, 0.05 um in y/x). That is small, but it makes 44b6 slightly worse than plain float, so re-check it on the confirmation replay. (b) Decision rule: one probe = best-known submission + the encoding. Keep it only if the public score does not drop (encoding a) or rises by >= 0.001 (plain float). With plain floats, revert on any unchanged score. (c) Lab gate: judge on 6bba plus the D-weighted per-embryo CI. Treat the 44b6 result as a single leak-group observation, and report the win rate among changed videos only. Do not claim +0.0018 as the transfer estimate. (d) Treat the float-aware linefit retune as low priority: it is tuned on the same in-sample tail, and B28's optimum was unimodal.
realistic_public_gain: +0.0007 to +0.0015 on an unseen embryo if the server keeps Float64 (the worse-localisation proxy says the gain survives or grows). 0 if the server rounds or truncates, provided the truncation-safe encoding is used. With plain floats and a truncating server, public could look flat while private loses about 0.004. At most about 7% of the 0.022 gap to 0.97, so ship it only as a bundle item.
